subject: SIG: Customer audit log export — S3 access pattern and retention

Cc: LogiBank Security <security@logibank.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG question — customer access to audit logs / S3 export pattern

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking the SIG intake. A few follow-ups from our security review team around audit logs that appear in the SIG: specifically we need to confirm how Redwood surfaces tenant event logs to customers, and whether there's a documented process we can include in our submission. Our checklist items: 

- Do you provide a persistent export of customer tenant audit events into customer-owned S3, or do you provide time-limited presigned URL exports?
- If presigned URLs are used, what is the max TTL and what are the signing/encryption constraints?
- Retention: what default retention do you enforce, and can customers request longer retention?
- Evidence: we need a sample of the log schema and a runbook we can attach to the SIG explaining the export flow and proof that logs include principal, timestamp, event_type, and request_id.

We are fine with a short redacted sample and a short runbook. Our target is to close this SIG section by EOD Thu 2027-04-08.

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Grant
Security Engineer, LogiBank

Hi all,

Thanks — replying with the technical details and attaching two artifacts: 'sig_s3_export_runbook_v1.pdf' (customer-facing runbook) and 'redwood_auditlog_sample_2027-04.ndjson' (redacted). Also included a short policy excerpt 's3-presigned-url-policy.txt' showing allowed TTLs. Summary below — happy to expand if LogiBank needs more detail.

Summary (short):
- Export options: We support two modes for tenant audit logs:
  1) Push-to-customer-S3: For enterprise customers with dedicated infra, Redwood can be configured to write daily/near-real-time compressed ndjson objects to a customer-owned S3 bucket using an assumed-role workflow. This requires the customer to provision an IAM role with a narrow write-only policy and supply the role ARN to Redwood.
  2) On-demand export via presigned URL: For self-serve customers we provide an on-demand export API that generates a presigned S3 GET URL for a zipped log bundle. This URL is time-limited.

- Presigned URL constraints:
  - Max TTL: 48 hours (configurable down to 1 hour).
  - Signing: URLs are V4-signed using our service principal; content is stored encrypted at rest using server-side AES-256 (SSE-S3) when in Redwood-controlled buckets. When delivering to customer-owned buckets via assumed role, object-level encryption follows the customer's bucket policy.
  - Access control: Presigned exports are single-use links tied to a signed export request and require the originating request ID. Links are logged and revoked automatically after expiry.

- Retention:
  - Default retention for hosted tenants: 90 days for full event payloads, with 13-month aggregated metadata retention for billing/usage metrics.
  - For Dedicated/Private customers we offer retention customization via a written agreement (up to 7 years with approved controls). Requests for >90-day retention on hosted plans are evaluated case-by-case; CS/Legal must approve and we maintain a retention exception register (see runbook, section 3).

- Log schema & evidence:
  - The attached sample contains the standard fields we provide: timestamp (ISO8601), principal_id (internal user/service principal), event_type, request_id (UUID), resource, outcome, and metadata blob. PII is redacted in samples.
  - The runbook describes the push-flow (assume-role handshake, object naming convention, verification via HEAD/GET), and the on-demand export flow with example cURL.

Next steps:
- I've attached the artifacts (redacted). Olivia — please confirm if the 90-day default + the presigned URL TTL of 48 hours is acceptable for your SIG. If LogiBank needs a push-to-customer-S3 configuration, we can start the IAM onboarding checklist (2–3 business days).

Attachments:
- sig_s3_export_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook; includes step-by-step onboarding checklist)
- redwood_auditlog_sample_2027-04.ndjson (redacted example)
- s3-presigned-url-policy.txt (policy excerpt)

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — this is exactly what we needed. The artifacts you attached are good; two quick follow-ups: 

1) For the push-to-customer-S3 flow, can you confirm the object naming convention so we can map to our processing pipeline? If possible show the example key pattern (bucket/prefix/yyyy/mm/dd/tenantid/events_YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz) — redacted tenant id is fine.
2) Our compliance team prefers presigned URL TTLs under 24 hours. Are you willing to lower the default max TTL to 24 hours for SIG customers (or make it configurable per-export)?

If you can confirm those two small items we'll mark this section of the SIG as answered. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Olivia
